utterances.text: Yes. You start in the morning what we call military briefing that becomes part of the routine of the mission. And we sat and hear a sit-rep for that day given by various assets of the UN. You hear military briefing, you hear civil police briefing and you hear civilian briefing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So by the time you actually arrived in Sector North, you did have quite a lot of information about the situation and what was going on, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I testified to that. I even came via west Slavonia where I was on the ground on the way to Sector North.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you look, please, at a document DB134, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour can I just say we haven't had a list of documents from Mr. Ackerman, it would help I think if by tomorrow morning we could be provided it so we can get them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There is only these two today that I just handed you a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have only been handed one, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You should have two documents, I don't know why the Prosecutor doesn't have them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document. It's an United Nations document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You'll notice that this document is dated 25 October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a report of the Secretary-General pursuant to paragraph 3 of Security Council resolution 713, and this is a report that would certainly have been available to you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To look at prior to undertaking your mission, correct?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, just by looking at it today, and I understand that the entire report is not here, I have selected pages, I can make the entire report available tomorrow if you want to look at all of it, but do you have any recollection as to whether you in fact read this as one of the UN documents you read prior to undertaking your assignment?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically, I would say to you in the earlier answer, yes as part of the briefing in terms of UN documents. I'm not sure this particular one was one I studied or can refer to readily the way I refer to my own documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When we look at the second page, page 456, and under the heading "situation on the ground," you'll see paragraph 8?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The current situation in regard to Yugoslavia is not only very serious but in addition it is in a constant state of flux and change, as regards both the political discussions under way and the situation on the ground. You were aware of that, were you not?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just read the statement, am I aware of the statement or what the statement refers to?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you aware of what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I'm just reading what this -- remember, I'm in New York. If I read it at all, I will read it exactly the way you're reading it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But when you arrived in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'hm?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you aware of this situation that's described, serious, constant state of flux and change, and so forth?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you go there with that impression in mind?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We expected to see a war zone and we saw one, as I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So what is the answer to my question? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there was a serious situation on the ground, yes, we were aware it was a situation on the ground. That it was going to stabilise as a result of the UN deployment is what we were looking for, not for a situation getting any other characteristic than what the report says, serious and in a state of flux.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The next sentence, earlier fighting in Slovenia having abated and died out in July, heavy fighting has since then persisted in Croatia, pitting on one side the Yugoslav national army, JNA and supplementary military units as well as irregular Serb forces against on the other side the territorial forcers of the Republic of Croatia as well as Croatian irregulars. Were you familiar with that proposition before you arrived or did you learn about it after you arrived?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt about it on the ground. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Civilian inhabited areas have persistently been subjected to direct fire, including from artillery and rocket batteries and indeed from armoured naval and air units. Were you aware of that at any point? And if so, when?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Increasingly, the first awareness I had of the hostilities on the ground was entry into Sector East through the confrontation line, where there were still combatants facing each other in both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this sentence that we just read, sir, speaks of fairly serious combat situation, direct fire, artillery, rockets, armoured naval and air units. In other words, full-blown war, right?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsellor you're asking me when I got aware of something, and I told you I'm aware of it on the ground as I get exposed to the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just asked you a different question?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know you asked me a different question but I'm telling you the difficulty answering your question. First I have to get where it is before answering your question. I cannot speak to a general thing and say, I am aware they were referring here or there because I answered you in the first place I wasn't aware, until I get there. So you must ask me where I was and what I was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, please ask me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Secretary-General reported civilian inhabited areas have persistently been subjected to direct fire including from artillery and rocket batteries and indeed from armoured and naval air units?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the answer to your question, this report is dated October, 1991. He may be talking about things that happened prior to my arrival.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm talking about. I don't care when it happened, I don't care where it happened. Do you accept that the Secretary-General is reporting that accurately?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know beyond what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, how can he answer that? He wasn't there, he's already said that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How can he answer that? He doesn't know whether it's accurate or inaccurate. He wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner is right, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that there had been this kind of serious armed combat going on in the state of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES KIRUDJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I got to the ground, as I moved from place to place, I got to learn of the details what happened, where, I arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to stop here, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. We will continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will continue tomorrow, Mr. Kirudja.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 9.00 here in the same courtroom. I thank you all. See you tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of February, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
